summary: The code is syntactically valid and runs, but it diverges substantially from the specified simulation task. It uses different parameter names, omits many required entities/behaviors/metrics, and does not implement validation criteria. There are also performance concerns (O(N*L) daily loops and O(N*HH) initialization). Some logic is inconsistent with the spec (e.g., availability not tied to inventory, no fines/denials), and reproducibility will fail with the provided 'seed' parameter.

issues.description: Required entities, attributes, and behaviors are incomplete or missing (e.g., Person lacks several attributes like sex, occupation, essential_worker, health_risk_level; missing behaviors like experience_fatigue_and_habit_decay, share_opinions_or_signals). Government lacks subsidy/distribution behavior. Media targeting/frequency not modeled. Only one Retailer is used.
issues.location: Classes Person, Household, Location, HealthAuthority, InformationSource, Retailer
issues.solution: Add missing attributes and behaviors per spec. Implement mask fatigue and habit decay, opinion sharing, government mask subsidies/distribution, media targeting/frequency, and multiple retailers with supply capacity and restock schedule.

issues.description: Metrics required by the spec are not computed (time_to_50_percent_adoption, peak_adoption, sustained_adoption_last_30_days, compliance_by_location_type, stockout_rate, inequality_in_adoption, policy_violations_per_capita, cost_per_percentage_point_adoption).
issues.solution: Track and compute all specified metrics. For example, compute time to 50% threshold crossing, peak adoption and day, last-30-days mean, per-location-type compliance, retailer-day stockouts, SES-based inequality (e.g., Gini or variance), policy violations per person, and public cost per percentage point adoption.

issues.description: Parameter names and usage do not align with the spec. The simulation expects 'simulation_duration_days' and 'seed', but the code uses 'time_horizon_days' and 'random_seed'. Many other parameters are ignored or renamed, e.g., mask_cost vs price_per_mask, restock_interval_days, supply_capacity_per_day, message_effectiveness, enforcement_level details.
issues.solution: Adopt spec parameter keys or map them consistently. Use 'simulation_duration_days' for time horizon, 'seed' for RNG seed, 'mask_cost' for price, implement 'restock_interval_days' and 'supply_capacity_per_day', apply 'message_effectiveness', 'mandate_effect_size', etc.

issues.description: Interactions are simplified and do not fully match the spec. Policy enforcement does not deny entry or levy penalties; it's not tied to Government penalty_amount. Market availability in decision logic is static and not tied to actual inventory.
issues.solution: Implement deny entry or apply penalties based on enforcement strictness and penalty_amount, track violations. Tie market availability to actual retailer inventories (e.g., probability of availability equals fraction of retailers with stock).

issues.description: Validation criteria are not implemented (stylized S-curve check, policy monotonicity sanity, extreme cases, convergence stability, reproducibility check).
issues.solution: Add post-run validation routines to check bounded adoption, inventory non-negativity, reproducibility with fixed seed, S-curve under specified conditions, monotonicity with enforcement, extreme case behavior, and convergence stability.

issues.description: Reproducibility will not work with the spec's 'seed' parameter because the code uses 'random_seed'. Counterfactual simulation resets 'random_seed' but ignores 'seed'.
issues.location: Simulation.__init__ and main() when constructing cf_params
issues.solution: Use 'seed' per spec (fallback to 42). Ensure both baseline and counterfactual use the same seed for reproducibility.

issues.description: Mask availability in decision-making is a fixed parameter and not derived from current inventory/stockouts. This decouples adoption decisions from supply constraints.
issues.solution: Compute market availability dynamically from retailer(s) inventory (e.g., fraction of retailers with stock or inventory per capita) and pass that value to decisions.

issues.description: Policy enforcement does not deny entry or fine non-compliant visitors; it only adjusts their propensities. Policy violations are not tracked.
issues.solution: Implement deny_entry_or_apply_penalty with penalties tied to Government.penalty_amount and track policy_violations_per_capita.

issues.description: Risk signal period and mode do not honor spec parameters (risk_signal_period_days, risk_signal_mode). The function uses a fixed 7-day period and exponential decay not specified.
issues.solution: Use risk_signal_mode ('exogenous') with period 'risk_signal_period_days' and amplitude from params; remove or parameterize decay.

issues.description: Initialization uses an O(N*HH) household lookup by scanning all households to assign each person. For N≈5000 this can be very slow.
issues.solution: Build a direct mapping from person_id to household_id when creating households, then use O(1) lookup.

issues.description: Location enforcement iterates over all persons for every location (O(N*L) per day). With N≈5000 and L≈200 this is 1M+ checks per day, likely slow for 120 days.
issues.location: Simulation.step (enforcement pass over all locations and persons)
issues.solution: Pre-sample visitors once per person based on mobility, then assign them to locations, or sample a subset of persons per location based on capacity and foot traffic without scanning all persons.

issues.description: Only a single Retailer is modeled while the spec requires multiple retailers, inventory restock interval, and supply capacity per day.
issues.solution: Instantiate 'retailer_count' retailers, implement restock_interval_days scheduling, and cap restocks by supply_capacity_per_day. Track stockouts per retailer-day for stockout_rate.

issues.description: Compliance by location type is not measured, and location policies are simplified to 'mandate'/'recommended'/'none' without policy_level/enforcement_strictness per type.
issues.solution: Add policy_level and enforcement_strictness attributes per location type as per params, and compute compliance_by_location_type metrics during visits.

issues.description: No modeling of subsidies (subsidy_amount) or cost accounting for cost_per_percentage_point_adoption.
issues.solution: Apply subsidy_amount to effective price in purchases and track cumulative public spending; compute cost per percentage point of adoption uplift.

issues.description: Mask fatigue and adoption decay without exposure are not modeled.
issues.solution: Add mask_fatigue and adoption_decay_without_exposure dynamics that reduce wearing propensity or habit strength over time without reinforcing signals.
